annotations.description: Playing basic Swamp instead of Gloomlake Verge on turn 1 is slightly suboptimal. Gloomlake Verge can only tap for B unconditionally (without controlling an Island or Swamp). By playing Gloomlake Verge first, it taps for B immediately. Then on turn 2, playing Watery Grave (which is an Island and Swamp) would enable Gloomlake Verge to also tap for U. If instead you play Swamp turn 1 and Gloomlake Verge turn 2, you get the same result — Gloomlake Verge sees the Swamp and can tap for both colors. So functionally, the sequencing doesn't matter much for turns 1-2. However, playing Gloomlake Verge first preserves more flexibility: if you draw another non-basic land that needs basics, having the basic Swamp still in hand is better. Playing the Verge first is marginally better since it keeps the basic Swamp available for future land drops where a basic might matter (e.g., against opposing effects that care about basics, or if you need to play a land that enters tapped unless you control a basic). This is a very small sequencing error.
annotations.actionTaken: Played basic Swamp on turn 1
annotations.betterLine: Play Gloomlake Verge on turn 1 (it taps for B unconditionally), preserving the basic Swamp for later flexibility

annotations.description: Casting Sunpearl Kirin on turn 2 main phase is suboptimal for several reasons. First, the player should play Hallowed Fountain from hand before casting spells to have more mana available in future turns and avoid missing a land drop. Second, Sunpearl Kirin has flash, meaning it could be held up and cast at end of opponent's turn to preserve information and flexibility. Third, casting it now with no other nonland permanents worth bouncing means the ETB trigger returns nothing, and playing it pre-combat when holding Kaito (which has ninjutsu) means the Kirin could have been used as an unblocked attacker to ninjutsu Kaito in. Playing Grim Bauble first would also be reasonable as it provides a target for Sunpearl Kirin's bounce ability later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sunpearl Kirin during precombat main phase on turn 2 without first playing a land from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Hallowed Fountain (paying 2 life or tapped), then either pass holding up Sunpearl Kirin with flash for opponent's end step, or cast Grim Bauble to develop the board with a future bounce target for Kirin. Keeping Kirin for a future turn where it can bounce a valuable ETB permanent or serve as a ninjutsu enabler for Kaito would be better.

annotations.description: Kaito is at 4 loyalty on the battlefield as a 3/4 Ninja creature during Haiku Analyst's turn. The opponent has Preacher of the Schism (2/4 deathtouch) on board, which is a major threat generating card advantage and tokens. Using -2 to tap Preacher and put two stun counters on it would neutralize this threat for multiple turns and allow Kaito to attack safely. Alternatively, using the 0 ability to Surveil 2 and potentially draw a card (if the opponent lost life this turn from Grim Bauble's -2/-2 trigger on the stack) would generate card advantage. The +1 emblem giving Ninjas +1/+1 is minimal value - Kaito is the only Ninja on board, making him a 4/5 instead of 3/4, and there are already two more Kaitos in hand (legendary, so can't deploy them as additional Ninjas easily). The -2 on Preacher of the Schism is significantly more impactful for the game state, neutralizing the opponent's only creature and main source of card/board advantage while still leaving Kaito at 2 loyalty.
